newsitem.title: USA: GCA Dec. coffee stock data seen mildly bearish.
newsitem.headline: GCA Dec. coffee stock data seen mildly bearish.

text.p: New York coffee futures are likely to ease a bit after monthly inventory data released late Wednesday showed an increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks, traders and analysts said.
Supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses rose in December by 63,000 60-kg bags, to 1,327,000 bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported late Wednesday.
Market participants had forecast a build up between 50,000 and 100,000 bags.
"It was very much in line with what we expected," one trader said. "But it may have a slightly negative impact because it has been such a strong market recently."
The port of Laredo, Texas, posted the largest gain in coffee stocks. Laredo stocks rose by 69,000 bags to 173,000 bags, the GCA said.
Inventories increased by 52,000 bags, to 204,000 bags in New York. However, warehouse stocks in New Orleans decreased in December, falling 48,000 bags to 481,000 bags.

But while many industry sources said the build up in stocks was to be expected with many Latin American countries' coffee harvests well underway, others had expected a decline in consumer coffee inventories during December after the latest drawdown in exchange-certified coffee stocks.

Coffee stocks in U.S. warehouses certified for delivery against CSCE futures fell by 9,070 60-kg bags in the week ended January 10, to 23,388 bags, the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange reported after the close Monday.
As of January 14, CSCE certified coffee stocks stood at 23,138 bags.
Analysts also noted that any bearish sentiment brought on by the monthly GCA data may be offset by a slowdown in Colombian coffee exports due to a dock workers strike.
The work stoppage by dock workers has paralyzed the 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports shipped out through the main Pacific coast port of Buenaventura, port operators said Wednesday.
The strike, which was called Tuesday night, led to an order from the National Federation of Coffee Growers' to avoid the port until the strike was resolved, coffee exporters said.

But while CSCE futures rallied Wednesday morning on the Colombian news, traders said anticipation of the GCA stock increase drove prices well off highs late in the session and may already be priced into the market.
CSCE most-active March delivery ended up 0.40 cents a lb Wednesday, to 122.60 cents, after peaking at 124.20 cents.
